title: Protocol for quantifying and modeling light scattering in coral microskeletons
author: Kramer, Jacques, et al.

steps.title: Bleach coral fragments
steps.instruction: Remove organic tissue and pigments by bleaching coral fragments in 5 % sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) and then rinse and dry them.

substeps.instruction: Place coral fragments in a well‑ventilated fume hood and submerge completely in 5 % NaClO solution in a glass or plastic container large enough for full submersion.
Bleach for 12–24 h at 25 °C; do NOT use NaClO concentrations >10 % to avoid damaging fine skeletal features.
Remove samples from bleach and rinse thoroughly with deionized water for 5 min, gently agitating to dislodge debris.
Leave corals to air‑dry at 25 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Extract OCT optical properties
steps.instruction: Run the MATLAB OCT extraction script, load calibration, select ROIs, and save attenuation (μ) and reflectivity (ρ) data for each TIFF file.

substeps.instruction: Open MATLAB R2024a and run the script OCT_coral_area.
When prompted, load the calibration file calibration_constants.mat.
Set the number of slopes for signal fitting (default: num_slope = 1) based on visual inspection of A‑scan heterogeneity; adjust if a high‑scattering superficial layer is evident.
Choose a TIFF file from the working directory (each file takes ~3–5 min to process).
In the displayed B‑scan image, click twice to define a horizontal region of interest (ROI) – left and right boundaries.

For each A‑scan within the ROI the script: extracts the A‑scan signal, calibrates reflectance using fitted a and b, identifies surface peak, noise floor, and exponential decay region, fits one or more exponential slopes to estimate the attenuation coefficient μ, and computes the reflectivity coefficient ρ from the intercept.
After processing the ROI, the script asks whether to select another ROI; answer “Yes” to analyse additional regions on the same image or “No” to move to a new file.

The script saves each figure in an automatically created folder “OCT_Optical_Analysis”, adds a white dashed line to the B‑scan indicating processed A‑scans, compiles all extracted data into a CSV filtered for focus quality (±150 μm from focal plane), and saves a PNG overlay showing all processed A‑scans on the original B‑scan.
Repeat the above for each TIFF file as required.
